content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the composition of the Earth's atmosphere
Explain how the atmosphere evolved over time
Describe how oxygen and carbon dioxide levels changed
Explain the role of photosynthesis in shaping the atmosphere

Human activities are changing the atmosphere:
CO₂ levels increasing (from ~280 ppm to >420 ppm)
Describe the composition of the Earth's early atmosphere.
The early atmosphere was very different from today
It was formed by volcanic activity
There was little or no oxygen
This composition was similar to the current atmospheres of Mars and Venus
Explain how oxygen became a major component of the atmosphere.
Early Earth had no oxygen in the atmosphere
Simple photosynthetic organisms evolved in the oceans (about 3.5 billion years ago)
Oxygen was released as a by-product
Over hundreds of millions of years, oxygen accumulated
Plants evolved and increased oxygen production further
The ozone layer formed, protecting life from UV radiation
Explain how carbon dioxide was removed from the early atmosphere.
Carbon dioxide was removed by several processes:
Some reacted to form carbonate ions
Converted it to glucose and other organic compounds
Marine organisms made shells from carbonates
When they died, shells accumulated on seabed
Dead organisms buried before complete decay
Heat and pressure over millions of years
Formed coal, oil, and natural gas
